solutions.latex:
$$y=x^3-3x^2+7$$

Cuts the $y$-axis when $x=0$

$\therefore$ $y$-intercept $=7$

Stationary points occur when $y'=0$

$$\begin{aligned}y'&=3x^2-6x\\3x^2-6x&=0\\3x(x-2)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=2\end{aligned}$$

When $x=2$,

$$\begin{aligned}y&=2^3-3\times 2^2+7\\&=3\end{aligned}$$

$$y''=6x-6$$

When $x=0$, $y''=-6$

When $x=2$, $y''=6$

$\therefore$ $(0,7)$ is a maximum turning point

$(2,3)$ is a minimum turning point

\exfigure{1356_q18_s1}

$$A=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\cos 2x\sin^4 2x\,dx+\left|\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\cos 2x\sin^4 2x\,dx\right|$$

$f(x)=\sin 2x$, $f'(x)=2\cos 2x$, $n=4$

$$\int f'(x)[f(x)]^n\,dx=\dfrac{1}{n+1}[f(x)]^{n+1}+c$$

$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\cos 2x\sin^4 2x\,dx+\left|\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\cos 2x\sin^4 2x\,dx\right|\\&=\dfrac{1}{2}\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}2\cos 2x\sin^4 2x\,dx+\left|\dfrac{1}{2}\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}2\cos 2x\sin^4 2x\,dx\right|\\&=\left[\dfrac{1}{10}\sin^5 2x\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}+\left|\left[\dfrac{1}{10}\sin^5 2x\right]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\right|\\&=\dfrac{1}{10}\sin^5\dfrac{2\times\pi}{4}-\dfrac{1}{10}\sin^5 0+\left|\dfrac{1}{10}\sin^5\dfrac{2\times\pi}{2}-\dfrac{1}{10}\sin^5\dfrac{2\times\pi}{4}\right|\\&=\dfrac{1}{10}+\dfrac{1}{10}\\&=\dfrac{1}{5}\end{aligned}$$

Since $2.5\%$ of orders are despatched within 10 days, 10 has a $z$-score of $-2$

$$\begin{aligned}z&=\dfrac{\bar{x}-\mu}{\sigma}\\-2&=\dfrac{10-46}{\sigma}\\-2\sigma&=-36\\\sigma&=18\end{aligned}$$

Since the discount will be given to the $5\%$ of customers who need to wait the longest, we need the score which correlates to a $z$-score of $1.65$

$$\begin{aligned}1.65&=\dfrac{x-46}{18}\\29.7&=x-46\\x&=75.7\end{aligned}$$

Customers who wait more than 76 days will receive a discount.

$$P(\text{Jonathan wins})=\dfrac{3}{10}+\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{3}{10}+\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{3}{10}+\ldots$$

We are required to find the limiting sum of a geometric series where $a=\dfrac{3}{10}$ and $r=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$$\begin{aligned}S_\infty&=\dfrac{a}{1-r}\\&=\dfrac{\frac{3}{10}}{1-\frac{1}{2}}\\&=\dfrac{3}{5}\end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
We need to maximise difference between the time taken for the bus and Lucas to reach $P$.

Let $T=T_B-T_L$

$$\therefore\ T=200+15\tan\theta-\dfrac{75}{2\cos\theta}$$

Stationary points occur when $\dfrac{dT}{d\theta}=0$.

$$\begin{aligned}T&=200+15\tan\theta-\dfrac{75}{2\cos\theta}\\&=200+15\tan\theta-\dfrac{75}{2}(\cos\theta)^{-1}\\T'&=15\sec^2\theta+\dfrac{75}{2}(\cos\theta)^{-2}\times(-\sin\theta)\\&=\dfrac{15}{\cos^2\theta}-\dfrac{75\sin\theta}{2\cos^2\theta}\\0&=\dfrac{15}{\cos^2\theta}-\dfrac{75\sin\theta}{2\cos^2\theta}\\0&=15-\dfrac{75}{2}\sin\theta\\\dfrac{75}{2}\sin\theta&=15\\\sin\theta&=\dfrac{30}{75}\\\theta&=0.4115168461\end{aligned}$$

\exfigure{1356_q33_s1}

$\therefore$ when $\theta=0.411$, $T$ is a maximum

$$\begin{aligned}\text{When }\theta=0.411\ldots,\ T&=200+15\tan\theta-\dfrac{75}{2\cos\theta}\\&=165.6306823\text{ seconds}\\&=2\text{ minutes and }45\text{ seconds}\end{aligned}$$

Lucas must leave at 8:02 am at the very latest to catch the bus.

Markers' Note: 8:03am was not awarded as Lucas will miss the bus by 15 seconds
